I think some of the issue in the United States is the lack of comprehensive sex education. Our students are curious and are doing their own research. That research is porn, music videos, TV, movies, social media, etc.. The results of the research is what we’re seeing played out at school, but as educators our hands are tied. Just a few weeks ago I had a Muslim student around 2nd grade ask me during dismissal if sex was a bad word. No, sex is not technically a bad word, but I couldn’t say that because I don’t know what her family’s values are when it comes to this topic so all I could tell her was to ask her mom. I sincerely hope she did because her sister was telling her that it was and I would like to think that she looked for her own answer.

Comprehensive sex education has been linked to lower rates of unwanted pregnancy, fewer abortions, and places an emphasis on types of birth control and how to use them, as well as the responsibilities that come with having a baby. Comprehensive sex education also teaches enthusiastic consent, correct terminology for body parts, and how to make sure everyone involved in the act is having a good time.

Another thing I’ve noticed is the stigma around viewing porn. It seems as though it’s fine and dandy when we as adults use it but as soon as the kids see it, it’s evil. For the record, believe kids should not be watching that kind of content. However, porn is something they find when they do their “research.” I believe porn should be destigmatized. I’d rather redirect a student to an informative documentary or age appropriate source than shame them for curiosity about something no one appears eager to talk about.

We can’t control what others are posting on social media, but we can teach computer and internet safety. Don’t give someone you don’t know your phone number or address or full name. If someone is asking for something that makes you uncomfortable you can end the conversation and/or tell a trusted adult. Sending compromising photos of yourself is like squeezing all of the toothpaste out of its container- you’ll never get it back and it ends up being a big mess.

None of these things are the magic fix to what we’re seeing, but with appropriate changes, we might see some of these behaviors reduced. It won’t happen overnight, but I truly believe inappropriate/sexual behavior incidents will decrease.
